title: Explanatory Note to the Equity Statement: The Two Credits That Build a Member's Equity
content:
Two things land in a member's equity account under Membership and Patronage Equity and they are not the same thing.

**The equity portion of the allocation** is the part of the declared patronage the class holds back, and it is credited at the same time the allocation is posted.

**The per-unit capital retain** is a capital contribution and not a share of earnings, and it is taken whether or not the board declares any allocation at all that year. A class that lists no streams takes no retain. The amount retained on a line is the qualifying units it is taken on multiplied by the class's per-unit retain rate, rounded to two decimal places.

**What the two have in common.** Both are credited to the same equity balance and both revolve back out on the same cycle, and neither is ever refunded on request, since equity is returned only by revolvement, retirement or transfer.

**At the ceiling.** Where the class has reached its maximum equity balance the retain is still taken but the equity portion of the allocation is paid in cash instead, so the ceiling limits retention of earnings and not capital.

**The class figures.** The retain rate, the streams the retain is taken on and the ceiling are the figures the class carries.

## A clause of this note no longer in force

The words "taken separately at the class's retain rate on the qualifying units of the streams the class lists" are **no longer in force**, and are set down only so that no reader applies them. The volume the capital retain is now taken on, the rate it is taken at and the weighting it carries are governed by the current basis, which is carried with the capital retain rules. The rest of this note, including the distinction between the two credits, their common cycle and the treatment at the ceiling, stands as clauses in force.

## A member reading two credit lines

A member whose class retains 70 per cent of the allocation and takes a retain on grain bushels sees, for one fiscal year, one credit from the equity portion of the allocation and a second credit from the capital retain. They are separate credits on separate bases, and a year in which the board declared nothing may still show the second and not the first.

**On a refund.** A member asking for the retain to be paid back because the season went badly is asking for something no class of Membership and Patronage Equity provides; equity comes back by revolvement, by retirement or by transfer and by nothing else.
